title: Code review agents without humans: 45% merge rate vs 68%, and most feedback is noise — contradicting the '80% of PRs autonomously' pitch
summary: A study analyzing 3,109 pull requests from the AIDev dataset tested the industry claim that automated code review agents (CRAs) can independently handle the bulk of open-source review work. The empirical reality is sharply different: PRs reviewed only by CRAs were merged 45.20% of the time versus 68.37% for human-only review — a 23-point gap — with markedly higher abandonment. Feedback quality was the core problem: 60.2% of closed CRA-only PRs fell into the lowest signal band (0–30% useful comments), and 12 of 13 review agents averaged signal ratios below 60%, meaning most automated comments were noise rather than actionable findings. The authors conclude CRAs should augment, not replace, human reviewers, directly contradicting vendor claims that bots can autonomously manage ~80% of PRs. For engineering leaders, this is a caution against removing humans from the review gate: low-signal bot review correlates with worse merge outcomes and can erode contributor trust and velocity even as it appears to add 'coverage.'
whyItMatters: Removing humans from the review gate in favor of CRAs is associated with worse outcomes — a 23-point lower merge rate and more abandoned PRs — so 'autonomous review' should be treated as unproven for the merge decision.
Most automated review comments are low-signal noise (12 of 13 agents below 60% signal), which taxes contributor attention and trust; coverage metrics for bot review can be actively misleading.
Vendor claims of handling ~80% of PRs autonomously are not borne out in this data, warranting skepticism in procurement and a focus on human-plus-agent workflows rather than replacement.
recommendedActions: Keep a human as the merge-decision authority; position review agents as triage and first-pass assistants, not autonomous gatekeepers.
Measure review-agent signal-to-noise (share of comments that lead to a change) and tune or disable bots that fall below a useful threshold.
Evaluate any review-automation vendor against merge rate, abandonment, and contributor-trust metrics — not just comment volume or 'PRs covered.'
risksAndCaveats: Based on open-source AIDev PRs; enterprise repositories with stronger conventions, gated CI, and known contributors may see different agent performance.
Correlational: low merge rates may partly reflect which PRs get routed to CRA-only review, not solely agent quality.
Preprint reflecting the specific 13 review agents available in early 2026; tools are improving quickly.
